doc.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Singers who are musicians versus singers who are not
summary: Why a vocalist like Rebecca Kilgore who thinks like an instrumentalist keeps a set moving.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: You had mentioned talking about her that it was nice to work with, as you described, a singer who’s a musician.
Are there singers that aren’t musicians?

There are singers who don’t play other instruments. They’ll know the chords on a piano, or how to transpose — musical knowledge that everyone should have — but they don’t think in instrumental terms. They’re not thinking okay the band has just played a slow tune and now they’re bringing me on, I’d better do something uptempo to bring the excitement level back up. They think okay, well I need this chord here, and then this chord here, and then lead me in here and I’ll come in at this tempo, and then bring it up slightly and you can play this— and they don’t think, by then you’ve lost the crowd. You’ve got to keep things going. I mean it doesn’t have to be hyper, but I don’t like long gaps between tunes, I don’t like discussing routines. I want to know what’s going to happen before we get on the stand. And that’s why a singer like Rebecca, she’s thinking that same way — well we’d better keep it moving. chords on the verse or the set up, she’ll say let’s just start on the chorus, guitar and brushes, I’ll just sing it. And it makes it easy, and it keeps things moving along. That’s where a musician who is a vocalist is very handy.
